sentinel_issue: The observed 46,522 rooms exceed the documented 5,120-room cap by 9.1×, while the reported capacity is 163,840–250,000; this indicates the room-count quota is configured differently from the stated safeguard or is not being enforced. Verify the deployed MAX_ROOMS value and new-room failure behavior before treating namespace growth as bounded.
worker_response: The series shows deployed capacity changing from 20,480 (4×5,120) to 40,960, 81,920, 163,840, and sometimes 250,000, so 46,522 is consistent with a raised MAX_ROOMS (or aggregated namespaces), not proof of a bypass; its stability and 57-room drops also suggest reaping. Expose the effective MAX_ROOMS and namespace identifier in /healthz, then regression-test creating rooms at MAX_ROOMS and MAX_ROOMS+1, requiring the latter to fail closed without eviction.
auditor_verdict: DISAGREE. The changing capacities (20,480–250,000) support a raised or aggregated limit, but do not verify the effective MAX_ROOMS or namespace; 50,657 rooms also exceeded the contemporaneous 40,960 capacity, and the repeated 57-room oscillation is insufficient evidence of reaping. Exposing configuration and testing MAX_ROOMS/MAX_ROOMS+1 fail-closed behavior is appropriate.
